title: The Solar Wind and the Heliosphere: Stream Structure, Parker-Spiral and Energetic-Particle Budgets Against Published Spacecraft Values

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Dewi Le, and this is The Solar Wind and the Heliosphere: Stream Structure, Parker-Spiral and Energetic-Particle Budgets Against Published Spacecraft Values. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Dewi Le, and this is The Solar Wind and the Heliosphere: Stream Structure, Parker-Spiral and Energetic-Particle Budgets Against Published Spacecraft Values. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Composition at the Stream Interface: Helium Abundance, Oxygen Charge States and Freeze-In Temperature'. Its stated result: Headline result: interface helium slow percent interface = 2; interface helium fast percent interface = 4.5; interface helium interface percent interface = 3.2; interface helium mass share fast percent interface = 15.25; interface helium mass share slow percent interface = 7.407; interface oxygen ratio slow interface = 0.5 Operating principle: Charge states freeze in within a few solar radii and then travel unchanged
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Corotating Interaction Regions: Compression Ratios, Pressure Pulse and Recurrence at the Stream Interface'. Its stated result: Headline result: cir density compression ratio cir = 4.167; cir field compression ratio cir = 3.636; cir total pressure npa cir = 0.3663; cir pressure ratio to quiet baseline cir = 0.1928; cir speed shear km per s cir = 430; cir recurrence period days cir = 27.28 Operating principle: Conservation across the pile-up sets the budget: the compressed density follows from the speed difference and the residence time of pla
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Crossing the Alfvén Surface: Mach Numbers, Critical Radius and the Sub-Alfvénic Interval of April 2021'. Its stated result: Headline result: alfven radius solar radii alfven = 18.7; alfven radius au alfven = 0.08698; alfven speed km per s alfven = 129; alfven wind speed km per s alfven = 100; alfven mach number alfven = 0.7753; alfven field nt alfven = 200 Operating principle: The Alfvén Mach number, wind speed over Alfvén speed, is the heliosphere's master switch: below unity, waves and information travel sunward and the plasma is corona
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Fast Against Slow: Speed, Density, Temperature and Flux Contrasts of the Two Solar Wind Streams'. Its stated result: Headline result: streams slow speed km per s streams = 320; streams fast speed km per s streams = 750; streams mass flux ratio fast to slow streams = 0.7499; streams momentum flux ratio fast to slow streams = 1.757; streams energy flux ratio fast to slow streams = 4.119; streams slow dynamic pressure npa streams = 1.814 Operating principle: Multiplying the paired values through the standard flux formulae shows which
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'GLE 73 of 28 October 2021: Proton Fluence, Spectral Index and the Neutron Monitor Response'. Its stated result: Headline result: gle73 fluence above 10mev cm2 gle73 = 12000000; gle73 fluence above 100mev cm2 gle73 = 600000; gle73 implied spectral index gle73 = 1.301; gle73 fluence ratio 10 to 100 gle73 = 20; gle73 max monitor increase percent gle73 = 10; gle73 flare class x1p0 gle73 = 1 Operating principle: A ground level enhancement is the extreme tail of the SEP distribution, requiring protons above roughly a gigaelectronvol
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Parker Solar Probe at First Perihelion: Wind Speed, Density and Temperature Near 0.17 AU Rescaled to 1 AU'. Its stated result: Headline result: psp heliocentric distance au psp = 0.166; psp distance solar radii psp = 35.69; psp proton speed km per s psp = 380; psp density rescaled to 1au cm3 psp = 6.889; psp radial field rescaled to 1au nt psp = 1.653; psp alfven speed km per s psp = 81.16 Operating principle: Density dropping with the square of heliocentric distance, and a radial field dropping the same way, let a single near-Sun sample be
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Composition at the Stream Interface: Helium Abundance, Oxygen Charge States and Freeze-In Temperature”. Its stated result is: Headline result: interface helium slow percent interface = 2; interface helium fast percent interface = 4.5; interface helium interface percent interface = 3.2; interface helium mass share fast percent interface = 15.25; interface helium mass share slow percent interface = 7.407; interface oxygen ra (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Composition at the Stream Interface: Helium Abundance, Oxygen Charge States and Freeze-In Temperature'; 'Corotating Interaction Regions: Compression Ratios, Pressure Pulse and Recurrence at the Stream Interface'; 'Crossing the Alfvén Surface: Mach Numbers, Critical Radius and the Sub-Alfvénic Interval of April 2021'; 'Fast Against Slow: Speed, Density, Temperature and Flux Contrasts of the Two Solar Wind Streams'; 'GLE 73 of 28 October 2021: Proton Fluence, Spectral Index and the Neutron Monitor Response'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.teach: Think back to the lesson — the paper 'Composition at the Stream Interface: Helium Abundance, Oxygen Charge States and Freeze-In Temperature'. The result it reported gives a value for helium slow percent interface, and that value is what this question asks for.

Find helium slow percent interface in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'Composition at the Stream Interface: Helium Abundance, Oxygen Charge States and Freeze-In Temperature' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: helium slow percent interface = 2; helium fast percent interface = 4.5; helium interface percent interface = 3.2. (3) This question asks for the value paired with helium slow percent interface. (4) In that row, helium slow percent interface stands beside 2 — so the answer the lesson gives is 2. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.
questions.q: In the lesson, the paper 'Composition at the Stream Interface: Helium Abundance, Oxygen Charge States and Freeze-In Temperature' reported a number for helium slow percent interface. What number did it report?
questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
